Factions.Name: Mordor
Factions.Description: Sauron's war-state uses expendable Orc soldiers, enslaved Snaga workers, and industrial siege to win through pressure and attrition. Protect its workers and avoid fighting on Mordor's terms.

Technologies.Name: Black Uruk Forging
Technologies.History: The Uruks of Lugburz are bred and mailed in the Black Mountain itself, and their harness turns aside the blows that kill lesser Orcs.

Technologies.Name: Engines of Morgoth
Technologies.History: Slave-crewed and iron-braced, the siege-engines of Mordor hurl everything the forges can spare until the walls come down.

Technologies.Name: Orc Cookhouses
Technologies.History: The cook-houses of the camp keep the Snaga at the wheel and the pick, boiling mash for the labour that feeds the war-machine.

Technologies.Name: War-drums of Angband
Technologies.History: The drums of the old forge-fortress still keep time in the camps of Mordor, and the Orcs swing their blades on the beat.

Heroes.Name: Sauron
Heroes.History: Sauron is a slow, powerful front-line hero whose crushing blows and Morgul Dread weaken nearby foes.

Heroes.Name: Gothmog
Heroes.History: Gothmog's command drives nearby Orcs to attack faster while his Morgul Dread slows enemies.

Heroes.Name: Khamûl
Heroes.History: Khamûl leads the hunt, helping nearby Orcs move faster and strike harder.

CivBonuses.Name: Snaga Thralls
CivBonuses.History: The Snaga are the slave-labour of Mordor, cheap and quick to breed, driven to work while Orc warriors are bred only for war.
CivBonuses.Description: Snaga Slaves are the only Mordor gatherers: cheap, fast to train, and defenseless. All Orc military omits gathering, forcing reliance on Snaga numbers and protection.

CivBonuses.Name: Blighted Desolation
CivBonuses.History: Where the shadow of Mordor falls the land itself sickens, and the harvests of intruders wither in blighted soil.
CivBonuses.Description: Enemy workers gathering inside Mordor territory suffer -15% gather efficiency (gathering only; no destruction, no build/move/combat effect). Mordor workers are immune; the effect ends when territory is reclaimed.

CivBonuses.Name: All-Seeing Eye
CivBonuses.History: From Barad-dûr the Eye of Sauron sweeps the lands, and none may hide long when its gaze turns upon them.
CivBonuses.Description: While Barad-dûr stands, the Eye searches enemy strongholds for about 40 seconds on an eight-minute cycle. Its arrival is announced globally; it does not reveal the whole map.

CivBonuses.Name: Hordes of Mordor
CivBonuses.History: The hosts of Mordor are numberless, bred in the pits of Udûn and driven from the East under the lash.
CivBonuses.Description: Mordor's maximum population limit is increased by 10%. The larger host relies on numbers, not higher-quality troops.

Structures.Name: Barad-dûr
Structures.History: The Dark Tower is Sauron's fortress and the seat of the Eye.
Structures.Description: Mordor's wonder sends a searching gaze across enemy strongholds every eight minutes while it stands; it does not reveal the whole map.
